chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Abu Al-Fazl, who said:

I was residing in Makkah, so I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'From where should I enter the state of Ihram for Hajj?' He said: 'From where the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) entered Ihram, from Al-Ji'ranah. Victories came to him in that place: the conquest of Al-Ta'if, and the conquest of Khaybar, and the Conquest [of Makkah].' So I said, 'When shall I depart?' He said: 'If you are a first-time pilgrim (Sarr), then when one day of Dhu al-Hijjah has passed, and if you have performed Hajj before that, then when five days have passed from the month.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْجِعْرَانَة: A specific location near Mecca designated as the Miqat for its residents
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّة: The twelfth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, during which Hajj is performed
key_terms.صَرُورَة: A first-time pilgrim who has not performed Hajj before

ai.seo_question: Where should residents of Mecca enter Ihram for Hajj and when should they depart?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes Al-Ji'ranah as the definitive Miqat for residents of Makkah, linking the ritual practice to the specific historical moment when the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) received the news of the conquests of Ta'if and Khaybar. It further distinguishes the timing of departure based on the pilgrim's experience, offering a nuanced legal ruling for first-time versus repeat pilgrims that reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Imams.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Safwan, from Abu Al Fazl who said,

‘I was in the vicinity of Makkah, so I asked Abu Abdullahasws: ‘From where should I be wearing the Ihraam for the Hajj. So heasws said: ‘From where Rasool-Allahsaww wore hissaww Ihraam, from Al-Ji’rana. Victories came to himsaww in that place – the victory of Al-Taif, and victory of Khaybar, and the (other) victories’. So I said, ‘When shall I go out?’ Heasws said: ‘If you were a first time Pilgrim, so when a day from Zil-Hijja passes by, and if you have performed Hajj before that, so when five (days) pass by from the month’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Safwan from abu al-Fadl who has said the following:

“I resided in Makkah and I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about wherefrom should I assume the state of Ihram for al-Hajj. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must assume the state of Ihram from where the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, did which is al-Ja‘ranah, which is the place where victory came to him several times like the victory of Ta’if, Khaybar and the Victory.’ I then asked, ‘When should I go out?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If it is your first al-Hajj, you can go out on the second day of Dhu al-Hajj ah, but if it is not your first al-Hajj, then you can go out on fifth of Dhu al-Hajj ah.’”
